body:
This PR introduces a conformal cubed sphere grid generation method that applies conformal mapping from an irregularly spaced grid (using exponential or geometric spacing) on the reference square to a more uniformly spaced grid on the cubed sphere panel, which covers 1/6th of the spherical surface. It also provides the option to further enhance the resulting grid's quality using the Ensemble Kalman Inversion (EKI) technique. EKI iteratively adjusts model parameters to optimize performance and accuracy, based on the comparison of model outputs with observational data. In our application, EKI is used to steer two key grid diagnostics---isotropy and the minimum cell width towards their desired values representing the "observational data" in our optimization process.

The primary motivation behind these improvements is to address the limitations imposed by the smallest corner cells, which significantly constrain the time step size in explicit time-stepping methods due to the CFL condition. By increasing the size of the smallest cells by a factor of two, this PR enables a proportional increase in time step size and computational performance.

Finally, this PR includes specialized functions designed to create clear and aesthetically pleasing visualizations of the cubed sphere grid and its individual panels, offering both 3D views and 2D projections.
title: Conformally map an irregularly spaced grid on the reference square to a more uniform grid on the cubed sphere panel
